claim: For every binary valuation of a single proposition on the simple undirected cycle \(C_n\), \(n\ge3\), ordinary modal equivalence at depth \(t\) agrees exactly with equality modulo reversal of the centered cyclic length-\(2t+1\) factors. At depth \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1\) the modal partition equals the orbit partition of the valuation-preserving dihedral subgroup, and this uniform depth is sharp for each \(n\ge6\), witnessed by \(V(p)=\{0,1,3\}\). Hence the Boolean modal algebra generated by this one valuation is \(\mathcal P(C_n)\) precisely for dihedrally asymmetric binary colorings; its minimum nonempty support is three for \(n\ge6\), and no such valuation exists for \(3\le n\le5\). For a disjoint union with \(c_n\) labeled \(n\)-cycles, full generation occurs exactly when each component word is primitive and reflection-asymmetric and distinct equal-length components have inequivalent dihedral word classes; the exact number of such valuations is \(\prod_{n\ge3}(2n)^{c_n}(b_n)_{c_n}\), with \(b_n\) the classical aperiodic chiral binary bracelet count. The bracelet count itself is explicitly recognized as known prior work.

correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed from first principles: the local reconstruction lemma yields exactly the centered substring reversal types at every modal depth; two-neighbor degree makes ordinary and graded signatures agree; omitted-one-vertex and omitted-adjacent-pair arguments handle even and odd circumference; the odd case uses step-orbit parity to synthesize a color-preserving reflection. The explicit three-marker gap pattern provides a sharp witness for every n>=6. Primitive periodic-word rigidity and orbit-stabilizer yield the disconnected census. The actual executable checks exhaustive words n=3..12, direct Boolean closure, disjoint cycle examples and witnesses through n=120. Finite checks corroborate but are not used as an infinite proof.

title: Sharp half-circumference modal stabilization on two-colored cycles

value.rationale: Determines a natural exact modal-depth invariant for every binary labeling of every finite simple cycle, including a sharp and attained universal stopping time. Proves the nontrivial coincidence of modal and automorphism-orbit partitions on the cyclic class despite its failure on general graphs, and settles one-generator existence and the component-multiplicity obstruction for disjoint unions. This gives a useful benchmark for finite model minimization and distinguishing formula depth rather than a one-off arithmetic constant.

verification.limits: Finite exhaustive and randomized tests corroborate but do not establish the universal mathematical theorem.
